syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic

concepts.learning_objective: State the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic and explain what the uniqueness of prime factorisation means.
Express a composite number as a product of powers of primes and use the factorisation to identify its factors.
Use the uniqueness of prime factorisation to decide whether numbers such as 4^n can end in 0 or whether an expression is composite.

topics.title: HCF and LCM by the Prime Factorisation Method

concepts.learning_objective: Find the HCF and LCM of two or three numbers from their prime factorisations.
Use HCF(a, b) x LCM(a, b) = a x b for two numbers and recognise that it does not hold in general for three numbers.
Apply the LCM to real-life problems about events that repeat at fixed intervals.

topics.title: Proving Square Roots of Primes Irrational

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the definition of an irrational number as one that cannot be written as p/q with integers p, q and q not 0.
State and apply the result that if a prime p divides a^2, then p divides a.
Follow and complete a proof by contradiction that the square root of a prime is irrational.

topics.title: Irrationality of Sums, Differences and Products

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether sums, differences, products and quotients involving rational and irrational numbers are rational or irrational.
Prove that expressions such as 5 - root 3 or 3 root 2 are irrational by reducing them to a known irrational number.

topics.title: Polynomials, their degree, value and zeroes

concepts.learning_objective: Identify polynomials and classify them as linear, quadratic or cubic by their degree.
Find the value p(k) of a polynomial and decide whether k is a zero of p(x).

topics.title: Geometrical meaning of the zeroes of a polynomial

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the zeroes of p(x) as the x-coordinates of the points where the graph of y = p(x) meets the x-axis.
Determine the number of zeroes of a polynomial from its graph and relate it to the degree.

topics.title: Zeroes and coefficients of a quadratic polynomial

concepts.learning_objective: Find the zeroes of a quadratic polynomial by splitting the middle term or using identities.
Use the relations sum of zeroes = -b/a and product of zeroes = c/a for ax^2 + bx + c.

topics.title: Forming a quadratic polynomial and expressions in its zeroes

concepts.learning_objective: Write a quadratic polynomial as k[x^2 - (sum of zeroes)x + (product of zeroes)].
Evaluate expressions such as alpha^2 + beta^2 and 1/alpha + 1/beta using the sum and product of zeroes.

topics.title: Zeroes and coefficients of a cubic polynomial

concepts.learning_objective: Use alpha + beta + gamma = -b/a and alpha*beta*gamma = -d/a for ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d.
Use alpha*beta + beta*gamma + gamma*alpha = c/a for a cubic polynomial.

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

topics.title: Representing situations as a pair of linear equations

concepts.learning_objective: Translate a real-life situation into a pair of linear equations in two variables.
Write a linear equation in two variables in the general form ax + by + c = 0 and identify a, b and c.

topics.title: Graphical method of solution

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the graphs of a pair of linear equations as intersecting, coincident or parallel lines and read the solution.
Classify a pair of linear equations as consistent, inconsistent or dependent.

topics.title: Comparing ratios of coefficients

concepts.learning_objective: Use the ratios a1/a2, b1/b2 and c1/c2 to decide the number of solutions of a pair of linear equations.
Find an unknown coefficient for which a pair of linear equations has a unique, no or infinitely many solutions.

topics.title: Substitution method

concepts.learning_objective: Solve a pair of linear equations by expressing one variable in terms of the other and substituting.
Model and solve word problems using the substitution method.

topics.title: Elimination method

concepts.learning_objective: Solve a pair of linear equations by making the coefficients of one variable numerically equal and eliminating it.
Model and solve word problems such as digit, income and speed problems using the elimination method.

topics.title: Quadratic equations and the standard form

concepts.learning_objective: State the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0) and identify its coefficients a, b and c.
Simplify a given equation to decide whether or not it is a quadratic equation.

topics.title: Representing situations as quadratic equations

concepts.learning_objective: Translate area, number and age situations into a quadratic equation in one variable.
Form a quadratic equation from a uniform speed, distance and time situation.

topics.title: Roots and solution by factorisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when a real number is a root of a quadratic equation and how many roots it can have.
Find the roots of a quadratic equation by splitting the middle term and equating each factor to zero.

topics.title: Word problems solved by factorisation

concepts.learning_objective: Solve number, geometry and cost problems by forming and factorising a quadratic equation.
Decide which root of an equation fits the situation and reject the inadmissible one.

topics.title: Discriminant, nature of roots and the quadratic formula

concepts.learning_objective: Use the discriminant b² − 4ac to decide whether the roots are distinct, equal or not real.
Find the roots of a quadratic equation using the quadratic formula.

topics.title: Equal roots and feasibility of situations

concepts.learning_objective: Find the value of an unknown coefficient for which a quadratic equation has equal roots.
Use the discriminant to decide whether a real-life situation is possible and find its values.

topics.title: Arithmetic progressions and the common difference

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise whether a list of numbers or a real-life situation forms an arithmetic progression.
Find the common difference of an AP and use the condition of equal successive differences.

topics.title: The nth term of an AP

concepts.learning_objective: Write an AP in the general form a, a + d, a + 2d, ... from its first term and common difference.
Use a_n = a + (n - 1)d to find any term of an AP.
Find which term of an AP equals a given number, or how many terms a finite AP has.

topics.title: Applications of the nth term

concepts.learning_objective: Find the nth term from the last term of a finite AP.
Determine an AP when conditions on two of its terms are given.
Model and solve real-life situations using the nth term of an AP.

topics.title: Sum of the first n terms of an AP

concepts.learning_objective: Use S = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d] to find the sum of the first n terms of an AP.
Use S = (n/2)(a + l) when the first and last terms of an AP are known.

topics.title: Applications of the sum of an AP

concepts.learning_objective: Find a term of an AP from the sums of its terms using a_n = S_n - S_(n-1).
Solve real-life problems that involve the sum of terms of an AP.
Reason about relationships between sums of different numbers of terms of an AP.

topics.title: Similar figures and similarity of polygons

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish similar figures from congruent figures and identify classes of figures that are always similar.
Apply the two conditions (equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides) for similarity of polygons.

topics.title: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales theorem)

concepts.learning_objective: State the Basic Proportionality Theorem and write the ratios it gives.
Use the Basic Proportionality Theorem to find unknown lengths in triangles and trapeziums.

topics.title: Converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem

concepts.learning_objective: Use the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem to decide whether a line is parallel to a side of a triangle.
Deduce mid-point results for a triangle from the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem.

topics.title: AAA and AA similarity criteria

concepts.learning_objective: Prove triangles similar using the AAA or AA criterion and use the resulting proportions.
Write the similarity of two triangles with the correct correspondence of vertices and sides.

topics.title: SSS and SAS similarity criteria

concepts.learning_objective: Prove triangles similar when their corresponding sides are proportional and find unknown angles.
Prove triangles similar using one equal angle with the including sides proportional.

topics.title: Applications of similar triangles

concepts.learning_objective: Use similar triangles to find heights and shadow lengths by indirect measurement.
Relate corresponding medians of similar triangles to their corresponding sides.

topics.title: Coordinates of a point: abscissa and ordinate

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the coordinates of a point to its distances from the y-axis and the x-axis.
Recognise that points on the x-axis have the form (x, 0) and points on the y-axis have the form (0, y).

topics.title: Distance formula

concepts.learning_objective: Use the distance formula to find the distance between two points with given coordinates.
Find the distance of a point (x, y) from the origin as the square root of x squared plus y squared.

topics.title: Applications of the distance formula

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether three points are collinear by comparing the distances between them.
Classify a triangle or quadrilateral from the lengths of its sides and diagonals.
Find a point, or a relation between x and y, for a point equidistant from two given points.

topics.title: Section formula for internal division

concepts.learning_objective: Find the coordinates of the point dividing a line segment internally in a given ratio m1 : m2.
Write the coordinates of a point dividing a segment in the ratio k : 1.

topics.title: Finding the ratio of division

concepts.learning_objective: Find the ratio in which a given point divides the segment joining two points.
Find the ratio in which a coordinate axis divides a segment and the point of intersection.

topics.title: Mid-point formula and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: Find the mid-point of a segment and points dividing it into equal parts.
Use the mid-point formula with diameters of circles and diagonals of parallelograms.

topics.title: Trigonometric ratios of an acute angle

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the opposite side, adjacent side and hypotenuse for an acute angle and define sin, cos and tan as ratios of these sides.
Use cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A, tan A = sin A/cos A and cot A = cos A/sin A.

topics.title: Finding all trigonometric ratios from one given ratio

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using similar triangles, that trigonometric ratios depend only on the angle, and that sin A and cos A never exceed 1.
Find the remaining trigonometric ratios of an acute angle from one known ratio using the Pythagoras theorem.

topics.title: Trigonometric ratios of 30, 45 and 60 degrees

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the values of the trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60° and how they are derived from geometry.
Evaluate expressions and solve simple equations involving the trigonometric ratios of 30°, 45° and 60°.

topics.title: Ratios of 0 and 90 degrees and solving right triangles

concepts.learning_objective: State the trigonometric ratios of 0° and 90°, identify which are not defined, and describe how sin A and cos A change from 0° to 90°.
Find the unknown sides and angles of a right triangle when one side and one other part are known.

topics.title: Trigonometric identities

concepts.learning_objective: Use sin²A + cos²A = 1, 1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A together with the angles for which each holds.
Simplify trigonometric expressions and prove identities by writing them in terms of sin and cos or by using the basic identities.

topics.title: Line of sight, angle of elevation and angle of depression

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the line of sight as the line from the observer's eye to the point viewed and use it to set up a right triangle.
Recognise the angle of elevation as the angle the line of sight makes with the horizontal when the object is above eye level.
Recognise the angle of depression as the angle the line of sight makes with the horizontal when the object is below eye level.

topics.title: Heights and distances using one right triangle

concepts.learning_objective: Find an unknown height or horizontal distance using tan or cot of a single angle of elevation.
Find the length of an inclined object such as a ladder, rope or kite string using sin or cos.
Account for the height of the observer's eye when finding the height of an object.

topics.title: Problems with two angles of elevation

concepts.learning_objective: Find the height of an object standing on another object using two angles of elevation from the same point.
Relate the length of a shadow to the Sun's altitude and solve problems on change in shadow length.
Find the distance moved by an observer when the angle of elevation of a fixed object changes.

topics.title: Problems with angles of depression

concepts.learning_objective: Use alternate angles to show that an angle of depression equals the corresponding angle of elevation.
Find distances such as the width of a river or the gap between two ships observed from a height.
Combine an angle of elevation and an angle of depression observed from one point to find the height of another structure.

topics.title: A circle and a line in a plane

concepts.learning_objective: Classify a line as non-intersecting, secant or tangent by the number of points it shares with a circle.
State the meaning of a secant and a tangent to a circle and recognise them in real situations.

topics.title: Tangent to a circle and its existence

concepts.learning_objective: Describe a tangent, its point of contact and how many tangents a circle can have.
Explain a tangent as the limiting position of a secant when the two ends of its chord coincide.
Reason that at most two tangents to a circle can be parallel to a given secant or line.

topics.title: Tangent perpendicular to the radius (Theorem 10.1)

concepts.learning_objective: Use the fact that the tangent at a point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
Calculate lengths in the right triangle formed by a radius, a tangent and the line joining the centre to an external point.

topics.title: Number of tangents from a point and length of a tangent

concepts.learning_objective: State how many tangents pass through a point inside, on or outside a circle.
Define and calculate the length of the tangent from an external point to a circle.

topics.title: Equal tangents from an external point (Theorem 10.2)

concepts.learning_objective: Prove and use the fact that the two tangents from an external point to a circle are equal in length.
Find angles formed by two tangents from an external point, the radii and the chord of contact.

topics.title: Applications: concentric circles and circumscribed figures

concepts.learning_objective: Find the chord of the larger of two concentric circles that touches the smaller circle.
Use equal tangents to relate the sides of a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle.
Find the sides of a triangle circumscribing a circle using equal tangent lengths and areas.

topics.title: Sectors and segments: minor and major regions

concepts.learning_objective: Define a sector and a segment of a circle and identify them in a figure.
Distinguish minor and major sectors and segments and relate their angles and areas.

topics.title: Area of a sector

concepts.learning_objective: Use the formula (θ/360) × πr² to find the area of a sector of angle θ.
Find the area of a major sector as πr² minus the minor sector, or with angle 360° − θ.

topics.title: Length of an arc of a sector

concepts.learning_objective: Use the formula (θ/360) × 2πr to find the length of the arc of a sector.
Find the perimeter of a sector as the arc length plus two radii.

topics.title: Area of a segment of a circle

concepts.learning_objective: Find the area of a minor segment as the area of the sector minus the area of the triangle.
Find the area of a major segment from the area of the circle and the minor segment.

topics.title: Applications of areas of sectors and segments

concepts.learning_objective: Find the area swept by clock hands and wiper blades using sector areas.
Find the area a tethered animal can graze in a field using sectors.
Solve problems where a circle is divided into equal sectors or equal segments.

topics.title: Surface Area of a Combined Solid: The Principle

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the basic solids (cuboid, cube, cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere) that make up an everyday object and which of their faces stay exposed.
Explain why the total surface area of a combined solid is the sum of the exposed surfaces of its parts and not the sum of their total surface areas.

topics.title: Surface Area of Solids Joined Together

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the total surface area of solids such as toys and capsules formed by joining a cone, cylinder or hemisphere of equal radius.
Account for flat faces that remain partly exposed, such as a cube carrying a hemisphere or a cone resting on a narrower cylinder.

topics.title: Surface Area of Solids with Depressions and Cavities

concepts.learning_objective: Find the surface area of a solid from which a hemisphere has been scooped out, adding the inner curved surface and removing the hidden flat face.
Find the surface area of a cylinder from which a conical cavity has been hollowed out and compare it with that of the original solid.

topics.title: Volume of a Combination of Solids

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the volume of a solid formed by joining two basic solids is the sum of their volumes.
Calculate the volume of objects such as toys, sheds and capsules formed by combining a cuboid, cylinder, cone or hemisphere.

topics.title: Volume of Solids with Parts Removed, Capacity and Displacement

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the volume or actual capacity of a solid from which another solid has been removed, such as a glass with a raised base or a pen stand with depressions.
Relate the volume of solids dropped into a full vessel to the volume of liquid that overflows, and count the number of objects needed.

topics.title: Mean of grouped data: class marks and the direct method

concepts.learning_objective: Find the class mark of a class interval and explain why it represents the class.
Calculate the mean of grouped data using the direct method.

topics.title: Assumed mean and step-deviation methods

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the mean of grouped data using deviations from an assumed mean.
Use the step-deviation method and judge when it is convenient.

topics.title: Mode of grouped data

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the modal class and the quantities used in the mode formula.
Calculate the mode of grouped data using the mode formula.

topics.title: Cumulative frequency distributions

concepts.learning_objective: Construct and read a less than type cumulative frequency distribution.
Construct and read a more than or equal to type cumulative frequency distribution.

topics.title: Median of grouped data and the empirical relationship

concepts.learning_objective: Locate the median class using n/2 and cumulative frequencies.
Calculate the median of grouped data using the median formula.
Apply the empirical relationship 3 Median = Mode + 2 Mean.

topics.title: Theoretical probability and equally likely outcomes

concepts.learning_objective: Decide whether the outcomes of an experiment are equally likely and explain why.
Use P(E) = favourable outcomes / all possible outcomes for experiments with equally likely outcomes.

topics.title: Elementary, sure and impossible events

concepts.learning_objective: Identify elementary events and use the fact that their probabilities add up to 1.
Recognise sure and impossible events and state that their probabilities are 1 and 0.
Use 0 <= P(E) <= 1 to judge whether a number can be a probability.

topics.title: Complementary events

concepts.learning_objective: Use P(not E) = 1 - P(E) to find the probability of the complement of an event.

topics.title: Drawing at random: playing cards, balls and numbered objects

concepts.learning_objective: Find probabilities of events when one card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards.
Find probabilities when one object is drawn at random from a collection of balls, discs or items.

topics.title: Experiments with two coins, two dice and repeated tosses

concepts.learning_objective: List the equally likely outcomes of tossing two or more coins and find probabilities from them.
Use the 36 ordered outcomes of throwing two dice to find probabilities of sums and other events.
